arxiv-2108-08791.title: Image Inpainting using Partial Convolution
arxiv-2108-08791.creator: Amey Kulkarni, Harsh Patel, Shivam Sahni, Udit Vyas
arxiv-2108-08791.description: Abstract Image Inpainting is one of the very popular tasks in the field of image processing with broad applications in computer vision. In various practical applications, images are often deteriorated by noise due to the presence of corrupted, lost or undesirable information.

arxiv-2204-13437.title: Regotron: Regularizing the Tacotron2 architecture via monotonic alignment loss
arxiv-2204-13437.creator: Efthymios Georgiou, Kosmas Kritsis, Georgios Paraskevopoulos, Athanasios Katsamanis, Vassilis Katsouros, Alexandros Potamianos
arxiv-2204-13437.description: Abstract Recent deep learning Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems have achieved impressive performance by generating speech close to human parity. However, they suffer from training stability issues as well as incorrect alignment of the intermediate acoustic representation with the input text sequence.

arxiv-2205-15643.title: From flocking to glassiness in dense disordered polar Active Matter
arxiv-2205-15643.creator: Matteo Paoluzzi, Demian Levis, Ignacio Pagonabarraga
arxiv-2205-15643.description: Abstract Abstract. Living materials such as biological tissues or bacterial colonies are collections of heterogeneous entities of different sizes, capable of autonomous motion, and often capable of cooperating. Such a degree of complexity brings to collective motion on large scales.

arxiv-2301-04785.title: Phase-shifted Adversarial Training
arxiv-2301-04785.creator: Yeachan Kim, Seongyeon Kim Co-corresponding authors who equally contributed to this work, Ihyeok Seo, Bonggun Shin
arxiv-2301-04785.description: Abstract Adversarial training (AT) has been considered an imperative component for safely deploying neural network-based applications. However, it typically comes with slow convergence and worse performance on clean samples (i.e., non-adversarial samples). In this work, we analyze the behavior of neural networks during learning with adversarial samples through the lens of response frequency.

arxiv-2402-04929.title: Source-Free Domain Adaptation with Diffusion-Guided Source Data Generation
arxiv-2402-04929.creator: Shivang Chopra, Suraj Kothawade, Houda Aynaou, Aman Chadha
arxiv-2402-04929.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel approach to leverage the generalizability of D iffusion M odels for S ource- F ree D omain A daptation ( DM-SFDA ). Our proposed DM-SFDA method involves fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model to generate source domain images using features from the target images to guide the diffusion process.

arxiv-2405-12204.title: Digitization and subduction of S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) gauge theories
arxiv-2405-12204.creator: Benoît Assi, Henry Lamm
arxiv-2405-12204.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Benoît Assi, Henry Lamm. The simulation of lattice gauge theories on quantum computers necessitates digitizing gauge fields. One approach involves substituting the continuous gauge group with a discrete subgroup, but the implications of this approximation still need to be clarified. To gain insights, we investigate the subduction of S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) and S ​ U ​ ( 3 ) SU(3) to discrete crystal-like subgroups.

arxiv-2406-01078.title: Unseen Visual Anomaly Generation
arxiv-2406-01078.creator: Han Sun, Yunkang Cao, Hao Dong, Olga Fink, {han.sun, olga.fink}@epfl.ch, cyk_hust@hust.edu.cn, hao.dong@ibk.baug.ethz.ch
arxiv-2406-01078.description: Abstract Visual anomaly detection (AD) presents significant challenges due to the scarcity of anomalous data samples. While numerous works have been proposed to synthesize anomalous samples, these synthetic anomalies often lack authenticity or require extensive training data, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2406-12027.title: Adversarial Perturbations Cannot Reliably Protect Artists From Generative AI
arxiv-2406-12027.creator: Robert Hönig, Javier Rando, Nicholas Carlini, Florian Tramèr
arxiv-2406-12027.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Robert Hönig, Javier Rando, Nicholas Carlini, Florian Tramèr. Artists are increasingly concerned about advancements in image generation models that can closely replicate their unique artistic styles. In response, several protection tools against style mimicry have been developed that incorporate small adversarial perturbations into artworks published online. In this work, we evaluate the effectiveness of popular protections—with millions of downloads—and show they only provide a false sense of security.

arxiv-2410-09725.title: Negative density-dependent dispersal of the mountain pine beetle in Alberta
arxiv-2410-09725.creator: Evan C. Johnson, Mark A. Lewis
arxiv-2410-09725.description: Abstract Abstract Understanding the mountain pine beetle’s dispersal patterns is critical for evaluating its threat to Canada’s boreal forests. It is generally believed that higher beetle densities lead to increased long-distance dispersal due to aggregation pheromones becoming repellent at high densities, causing beetles to seek areas with less competition.

arxiv-2502-09211.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jakob Johannes Bauer 1, Thomas Eiter 2, Nelson Higuera Ruiz 2, Johannes Oetsch 3. Visual Question Answering (VQA) is a challenging problem that requires to process multimodal input. Answer-Set Programming (ASP) has shown great potential in this regard to add interpretability and explainability to modular VQA architectures.

arxiv-2502-18499.title: Mechanistic Understanding of Language Models in Syntactic Code Completion
arxiv-2502-18499.creator: Samuel Miller, Daking Rai, Ziyu Yao
arxiv-2502-18499.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Miller, Daking Rai, Ziyu Yao. Recently, language models (LMs) have shown impressive proficiency in code generation tasks, especially when fine-tuned on code-specific datasets, commonly known as Code LMs. However, our understanding of the internal decision-making processes of Code LMs, such as how they use their (syntactic or semantic) knowledge, remains limited, which could lead to unintended harm as they are increasingly used in real life.

arxiv-2509-18179.title: The Describe-Then-Generate Bottleneck: How VLM Descriptions Alter Image Generation Outcomes Thanks: Sports Vision Research
arxiv-2509-18179.creator: Sai Varun, Kodathala, Rakesh, Vunnam
arxiv-2509-18179.description: Abstract With the increasing integration of multimodal AI systems in creative workflows, understanding information loss in vision-language-vision pipelines has become important for evaluating system limitations. However, the degradation that occurs when visual content passes through textual intermediation remains poorly quantified.

arxiv-2512-07166.title: When Privacy Meets Recovery: The Overlooked Half of Surrogate-Driven Privacy Preservation for MLLM Editing
arxiv-2512-07166.creator: Siyuan Xu, Yibing Liu, Peilin Chen, Yung-Hui Li, Shiqi Wang, Sam Kwong
arxiv-2512-07166.description: Abstract Privacy leakage in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has long been an intractable problem. Existing studies, though effectively obscure private information in MLLMs, often overlook the evaluation of the authenticity and recovery quality of user privacy. To this end, this work uniquely focuses on the critical challenge of how to restore surrogate-driven protected data in diverse MLLM scenarios.

pmc-11476101.title: Physician preferences for Online and In-person continuing medical education: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11476101.creator: Michael R. Mueller, Ivana T. Croghan, Darrell R. Schroeder, M. Nadir Bhuiyan, Ravindra Ganesh, Arya B. Mohabbat, Sanjeev Nanda, Elizabeth C. Wight, Deb L. Blomberg, Sara L. Bonnes
pmc-11476101.description: BackgroundThe worldwide market for continuing medical education (CME) was severely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, which precipitated an increase in web-based CME course attendance. Virtual education methods may be effective for engaging learners and changing behaviors. However, more information is needed about physician preferences for in-person vs. livestreamed CME courses in the postpandemic era.

pmc-12364571.title: Characterizing internal models of the visual environment
pmc-12364571.creator: Micha Engeser, Susan Ajith, Ilker Duymaz, Gongting Wang, Matthew J Foxwell, Radoslaw M Cichy, David Pitcher, Daniel Kaiser
pmc-12364571.description: Despite the complexity of real-world environments, natural vision is seamlessly efficient. To explain this efficiency, researchers often use predictive processing frameworks, in which perceptual efficiency is determined by the match between the visual input and internal models of what the world should look like.

pmc-13381618.title: Deep learning model to generate patient-specific pulmonary vein isolation lines from successful atrial fibrillation ablation cases: a proof-of-concept study
pmc-13381618.creator: Kazuo Sakamoto, Takeshi Tohyama, Hirotake Yokoyama, Tsukasa Watanabe, Tomomi Nagayama, Yasushi Mukai, Shunsuke Kawai, Daisuke Yakabe, Hiroshi Mannoji, Kazuhiro Nagaoka, Atsushi Tanaka, Mitsutaka Yamamoto, Kiyohiro Ogawa, Takeshi Mikami, Shujiro Inoue, Susumu Takase, Kei Inoue, Kazuya Hosokawa, Koji
pmc-13381618.description: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is an established standard ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), however, AF recurrence remains a major clinical challenge. We developed a deep learning model to generate patient-specific PVI lines on pre-ablation 3D voltage maps, using lesion sets from successful AF ablation cases with documented freedom from recurrence for more than one year as ground truth.

pmc-13392243.title: Tubulin autoregulation tunes microtubule dynamics to support multicellular architecture and viability
pmc-13392243.creator: Ana C Almeida, Chahrazed Lacheheub, Ivana Gasic
pmc-13392243.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers dynamically assemble into microtubules, key cytoskeletal elements involved in intracellular trafficking, cell adhesion, and division. The availability of free tubulins regulates the synthesis of new subunits. In response to excessive soluble αβ-tubulins, tetratricopeptide protein 5 (TTC5) selectively recognizes nascent tubulins at the ribosome, recruiting downstream effectors that degrade their encoding messenger RNAs, in a process known as tubulin autoregulation. Despite its well-characterized molecular framework, the biological relevance of this regulatory pathway remains unknown.

pmc-13452923.title: Sex-dependent bioactive lipid mediator profiles in multiple sclerosis
pmc-13452923.creator: Wing Hee Fung, Serhii Chornyi, Menno M Schoonheim, Bernard MJ Uitdehaag, Joep Killestein, Eva MM Strijbis, Gijs Kooij
pmc-13452923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPathophysiological drivers of sex differences in multiple sclerosis (MS) remain unclear. Potential candidates include bioactive lipid mediators (LMs), which are pivotal regulators of neuro-inflammatory responses.ObjectiveTo investigate sex-dependent LM differences in MS.MethodsPlasma lipids were measured using targeted HPLC-MS/MS in a birth-year MS cohort (N = 410; n = 285 MS, n = 169 RRMS, n = 80 SPMS and n = 36 PPMS).
